gitCommit.body:
Epic C PR1 — item dispositions + Not-Yet (defer) (#248)

* spec: Epic C gentle-affordances design (pause / Not-Mine / Not-Yet / session undo)

Design spec for the gentle-affordances cluster (purses-z76, purses-1an,
purses-x5u, purses-2f3f). Owner forks settled; data model = a curator-scoped
item_dispositions table governing triage-queue eligibility. Discovered latent
bug filed as purses-4bhh (sessions_active_unique over-enforces).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Pbw6ZGrY8VvxyvbAEDpKjq

* spec: fold 7-persona adversarial review into Epic C design

BLOCK resolved (pairing exclusion is load-bearing — disposed items are NOT
auto-excluded from selectNextPair). Folded: disposed<=>untriaged boundary
invariant (409 + clear-on-triage), cross-collection IDOR via item-capability
guard, per-item purge erasure vector, AA ink-on-chip fix + contrast gate,
count-shaming progress cue removal, pause/New-Session 4bhh gating, co-member
IDOR + idempotency + undo-survives-refresh tests, six-affordance layout contract.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Pbw6ZGrY8VvxyvbAEDpKjq

* plan: Epic C PR1 (item_dispositions + Not-Yet) task-by-task

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Pbw6ZGrY8VvxyvbAEDpKjq

* feat(db): item_dispositions table + domain types (Epic C PR1)

* feat(repo): ItemDispositionRepository with upsert/delete + DB tests (Epic C PR1)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Pbw6ZGrY8VvxyvbAEDpKjq

* feat(api): DispositionController + disposed<=>untriaged 409 invariant (Epic C PR1)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Pbw6ZGrY8VvxyvbAEDpKjq

* fix(erasure): delete item_dispositions on item/collection/account purge (Epic C PR1)

The item_dispositions FK has no ON DELETE CASCADE, so a leftover disposition
row blocked the parent item/collection hard-delete with a 23503 violation.
Wire ItemDispositionRepository erasure (tx-bound) into all three deletion
services BEFORE the parent row is hard-deleted:
- ItemPurgeService: deleteByItem before ItemRepository.hardDelete
- CollectionPurgeService: deleteByCollection before hardDeleteByCollection
- AccountDeletionService: deleteByCurator in the Phase-2 curator-private tx

Each integration test now seeds a disposition and asserts it is gone after
the purge/deletion (account-deletion covers both the owned-collection and
borrowed curator-private paths).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Pbw6ZGrY8VvxyvbAEDpKjq

* feat(api): /collections/[id]/dispositions routes with IDOR guards (Epic C PR1)

POST/GET on /dispositions and DELETE on /dispositions/[itemId]. POST/DELETE
resolve the item via requireApiItemCapability("preferences:write") then assert
item.collectionId === params.id (404 on mismatch — no cross-collection oracle).
GET uses requireApiCollectionAccess and scopes the list to session.user.id.
curatorId is always session.user.id, never from the body.

Dispositions are keyed (itemId, curatorId), so a co-member's DELETE/GET only
touches/reads their own rows — the co-member IDOR is closed by construction.

Registers the 3 new route+method cases in the route-authz-enumeration backstop.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Pbw6ZGrY8VvxyvbAEDpKjq

* feat: selectTriageItem queue-eligibility pure function (Epic C PR1)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Pbw6ZGrY8VvxyvbAEDpKjq

* fix(sort): exclude disposed items from pairing; clear disposition on triage (Epic C PR1)

selectNextPair now filters set_aside/deferred items out of pairing candidates
(a disposed item has no preference row, so the score-sort scored it ?? 0 and
treated it as eligible). compare/page.tsx fetches the curator's dispositions and
passes them in. The decisions route clears any disposition on a triage decision,
keeping the disposed<=>untriaged invariant. Uses DispositionController.bringBack
(not the repo directly) to satisfy the src/app no-restricted-imports rule.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Pbw6ZGrY8VvxyvbAEDpKjq

* feat(triage): Not-yet defer affordance + patient-waiting + ceiling-free progress (Epic C PR1)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Pbw6ZGrY8VvxyvbAEDpKjq

* test(e2e): Not-yet defer flow across tablet/phone/desktop (Epic C PR1)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Pbw6ZGrY8VvxyvbAEDpKjq

* test(e2e): sync sort-session triage assertions to ceiling-free copy (Epic C PR1)

Task 8 replaced the triage H1 'Triage' with 'How do you feel about this one?'
and the '{n} of {N}' progress with '{n} decided so far'. Update the 5 heading
assertions and 2 progress assertions in sort-session.spec.ts to match — same
test intent (triage renders; progression past item 1).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Pbw6ZGrY8VvxyvbAEDpKjq

* fix(sort): atomic clear-on-triage + disposed-exclusion DB proof + copy/a11y fixes (Epic C PR1 whole-branch review)

A. Wrap the decisions route's three writes (event insert, preference recalc,
   triage-only disposition clear) in a single withTransaction so a partial
   failure can't leave an item both ranked and disposed (disposed<=>untriaged).
   Capture userId once — tx-closure loses the session.user narrowing.
B. Add un-mocked DB proof (disposition-exclusion.integration.test.ts) that a
   deferred item is absent from the real compare path AND from preferences,
   while A/B still pair (spec §8).
C. DeferControl busy label: "Setting aside…" → "Just a moment…" (PR2 set_aside
   vocabulary was leaking into the PR1 defer action).
D. DESIGN.md: a "deferred" (not "set-aside") item resurfaces.
E. Add role="status" to the patient-waiting banner so it's announced on refresh.

Tests: +ATOMIC rollback test (FAIL on non-tx route, PASS on tx route),
+disposition-exclusion suite, +DeferControl busy-label test, +triage banner
role=status assertion. 21 unit + 12 DB pass; build + lint clean.

row blocked the parent item/collection hard-delete with a 23503 violation.

services BEFORE the parent row is hard-deleted:
- ItemPurgeService: deleteByItem before ItemRepository.hardDelete
- CollectionPurgeService: deleteByCollection before hardDeleteByCollection

borrowed curator-private paths).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Pbw6ZGrY8VvxyvbAEDpKjq

* feat(api): /collections/[id]/dispositions routes with IDOR guards (Epic C PR1)

POST/GET on /dispositions and DELETE on /dispositions/[itemId]. POST/DELETE
resolve the item via requireApiItemCapability("preferences:write") then assert
item.collectionId === params.id (404 on mismatch — no cross-collection oracle).
GET uses requireApiCollectionAccess and scopes the list to session.user.id.
curatorId is always session.user.id, never from the body.

Dispositions are keyed (itemId, curatorId), so a co-member's DELETE/GET only
touches/reads their own rows — the co-member IDOR is closed by construction.
